blindSummary:
This state/province recorded 4 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — the same absolute count as the neighbouring unit that showed the dataset's sharpest deterioration. Against a population of ~4 million this yields approximately 1.0 killings per million per year, roughly 2.6 times the national ~0.38 per million and among the highest rates in the federation. The state/province is part of the country's worst-affected region, which absorbed 38 of 80 national killings (47.5%) in 2025.

On rate, this state/province runs at roughly 2.6 times the national per-million figure: a comparable neighbouring unit with half the absolute count on a similar population (~0.61 per million) illustrates how the regional concentration compresses onto smaller denominators here. The victim profile — young, Black, poor, from this region — concentrates risk on individuals who present visibly in public space.

No state/province-specific legal or ordinance evidence was found; the elevated exposure is driven entirely by the violence dataset, not by any local statute.
blindSourceSummaries: National news report (26 Jan 2026) on the 9th edition of the trans-movement association's dossier: 80 killings of trans and travesti people nationwide in 2025, down 34% on 2024, still the world's highest; the 2025 state counts range from 8 at the top of the regional leaders down through 7s and 5s, with this state/province in the group recording 4; 1,261 killings cumulatively 2017-2025 (~140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, 70% Black, 67.5% killed outside state capitals.

Another national broadcaster's dossier summary: this country is 'the country that kills most trans people and travestis'; the victim profile is young, Black, poor and concentrated in the worst-affected region, with community life expectancy of about 35; killings occur mostly in public places, at night, with exceptional cruelty, and are routinely mis-recorded by authorities; the 2024 regional panorama shows the top units ranging from 6 to 16 killings.
